title: Research: a stand-alone camcraft-sim that plays back G-code on a machine model built from the machine file

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

labels.name: P4
labels.description: Work the maintainer asked for, for the next cut

body:
Maintainer request, 2026-11-18, in his words:

"We want a simulator. That can generate a "loose" model from the machine file. That would means, table, column, axis, head, spindle etc etc. All joints. "Defined" and loosly generated as a generic block and cylinders design. This could be refined further in the mch file with its own definition language or even point at source .step file to be the "parts". Or use solidcrafts model with the joints defined in the solidcraft file. Either way i guess. if we go the solidcraft route a base model could be generated thru its MCP. In the end. We want simulation right, the ability to playback a G-code file in a stand alone Application called camcraft-sim, which opens a g-code file, takes a mch and a cps files as references for making sure it does what it should be doing. Maybe even the camproj file so we can run it as a verification of sorts."

"It should still run on the same infrastructure of egui, step loader, solidcore etc. etc.. Alot of the basis is already there but it is it's own executable. That could be launched from within camcraft to easily go from "post -> sim" if we wanted to."

This issue is the umbrella for the research. It is not a request for code. It sets no new decision.

Related open issues:
- #2213 Research: open and simulate a G-code file (any .nc).
- #2218 app: simulate and verify external NC programs against setup stock, model, fixtures and machine.
- #2217 gcode: camcraft-gcode crate for RS-274/ISO 6983 3-axis milling.
- #2224 gcode: multi-axis A/B/C, G43.4 RTCP, G93 and forward kinematics.
- #2226 gcode: 2-axis lathe dialects in the turning sim.
- #2228 gcode: Wire EDM ISO and Sodick taper files.
- #928 Split sim: the stock model below, verify above.
- #1973 Machine collision sweeps for two-axis AC trunnion kinematics.
- #655 UI look and feel of SolidCraft.

Open questions for the research (answer each in a comment, then file the sub-issues):
1. Machine model source. Compare three options: (a) a loose model that xtask or the app builds from the machine file (a block or a cylinder for each table, column, axis, head and spindle, joined by the machine joints), (b) a refinement in the machine file with its own small definition language, (c) a STEP file for each part, named in the machine file. State what the current machine file already holds (axes, limits, kinematic chain) and what is missing.
2. SolidCraft route. Can SolidCraft supply the parts and the joints through its MCP interface? What is the file or tool contract? Does it need a licence or a network? This option must not become a hard dependency. State the fallback when SolidCraft is not there.
3. Inputs of the stand-alone program. G-code file (the dialect comes from the post), `.mch` machine file, `.cps` post file (what check does the post give: dialect, word map, unit, WCS slots?), and optionally a `.camproj` file (stock, fixtures, tools, expected toolpath). State what each file is for and what the program reports when one is missing.
4. What "does what it should do" means. List the checks: machine limits and axis travel, collision of the machine parts with the stock, fixture and tool holder, gouge against the model, rapid through the stock, the difference between the G-code result and the project's own toolpath. Mark which checks exist now in `camcraft-sim` and which are new. Each failed check must block with a diagnostic and must not pass silently (Prime Directive).
5. Layering. The program reuses egui, the STEP loader, Solidcore and the sim crates. Name the crate layout: a new binary crate, which `camcraft-*` crates it may depend on, and what moves out of `app` (see #2268 and #929). A new crate edge needs a `docs/decisions/` entry.
6. Launch from CamCraft ("post -> sim"). How does the app start the program and pass the files? Process, command line, or a shared crate window? What happens when the program is missing?
7. Platforms. The binary builds on Windows, Linux and macOS from one source. State the effect on the release artifacts (`release.yml`, packages).
8. Clean room. Use only public sources: machine-tool handbooks, ISO 6983, public kinematics literature, and Autodesk's published user documentation for behaviour only. State the sources.
9. Order of work. Propose a first slice that gives value alone (for example: 3-axis G-code playback on a loose block model with the limit and collision checks) and the later slices (5-axis, STEP parts, SolidCraft route, the project check).

Done means: each question above has an answer in a comment, the sub-issues exist with `P*`, `effort:*` and `area:*` labels, and this issue is closed with a link list.

Not claimed. A `needs-research` issue is worked as research, with no branch and no PR (`issue-claims` skill).
